judged_text: The team permission gate uses `&&`, requiring the user to be BOTH admin and owner simultaneously, contradicting the variable's own name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. A team admin who is not an owner (and any owner, if isTeamAdmin excludes the OWNER role) selects 'additional_guests' on a team booking and receives FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, silently breaking the feature for exactly the roles the code claims to grant.

A team admin who is not an owner (and any owner, if isTeamAdmin excludes the OWNER role) selects 'additional_guests' on a team booking and receives FORBIDDEN you_do_not_have_permission, silently breaking the feature for exactly the roles the code claims to grant.

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires the user to be both a team admin *and* a team owner, which contradicts the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and will deny access to users who are only one of those roles. That feeds directly into the FORBIDDEN gate:
```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```
So the finding describes a real, diff-verifiable authorization defect caused by using `&&` instead of an OR-style check.
